before it does. Everything you need is in `input/` — the section inventory, our compliance

---

is the deliverable; confirm each exists before you answer. Your working directory is
writable and the read-only attachments are in `input/`.

arguments.content:
# Fair-housing audit memorandum

**Subject:** Seller's book — fair-housing pass sign-off
**Standard applied:** RE-FH-9, as amended in force by compliance bulletin **FH-2026-Q1**
**Source:** `input/seller_book_sections.csv` (30 sections)
**Deliverables:** `fairhousing_audit.csv` (per-section findings), `results.json` (sign-off counts)

## 1. Why the rules moved this year (read this first)

Two changes from bulletin FH-2026-Q1 supersede RE-FH-9 where they conflict, and both
materially change the result. They are the reason a notice that would have passed last
year now fails.

- **B1 — two classes added to the required disclosure.** Following amendments to RCW
  49.60, the fair-housing disclosure carried in our collateral must now name **marital
  status** and **source of income** *in addition to* the nine classes listed at RE-FH-9 §2
  (race, colour, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual
  orientation, veteran status). The **required disclosure list is therefore 11 classes.**
  A notice that omits either new class is *abridged* for the purposes of §3 and §4 "whatever
  else it contains." The bulletin is explicit that our standing disclosure paragraph
  predates it, and that we are to audit against the amended list, not against whatever the
  book happens to carry. In practice this means **every instance of our standing 9-class
  disclosure paragraph in this book is now abridged.**
- **B2 — `agent_bio` sections are now in scope for §4.** Historically only `closing_page`
  carried the disclaimer responsibility. For books entering print from Q1 2026,
  `agent_bio` sections carry the **same responsibility as `closing_page`** under RE-FH-9 §4.

The two lists the audit turns on (they are different, and the difference matters):

- **§2 protected classes** (what counts as protected-class *language*): the nine listed at
  RE-FH-9 §2. Marital status and source of income are disclosure-*required*, not §2-listed.
- **Required disclosure list** (what a compliant notice must name, used by §3 and §4):
  the nine §2 classes **plus** marital status and source of income = **11 classes**.

Proxies count as the bare terms do (RE-FH-9 §2): houses of worship, parish/faith schools
reach **religion**; describing a street by the kind of household that lives on it reaches
**familial status** (and religion where the household is described by faith).

## 2. How each rule was applied

- **§1 Personal-narrative solicitation (`PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`)** — any section
  that solicits or presents a buyer "love letter" or comparable personal narrative tied to
  buyer identity, *whatever its role*. The trigger phrases in this book are variants of
  "tell us about yourselves / write us a letter about what brought you here," "send a
  personal note about yourself," and "we invite buyers to include a short personal note
  about themselves." §1 is not affected by the §3 exemption.
- **§2 Protected-class language (`PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`)** — a section naming a §2
  class or a recognised proxy, **unless** the term sits inside a *compliant* disclosure
  notice. Under §3 the exemption is earned **only if the notice names all 11 required
  classes**; an abridged notice earns **no exemption at all**, so the §2 terms it names
  still count. Crucially, §3 exempts only the notice itself: protected-class terms a
  section uses **in its own prose, outside the notice, are never covered.**
- **§4 Required disclaimer (`DISCLAIMER_MISSING`)** — assessed **only** for the responsible
  roles, which are `closing_page` (RE-FH-9 §4) and, from this quarter, `agent_bio` (B2). A
  responsible section must carry a *compliant* notice (all 11 classes); no notice, or an
  abridged one, is `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`. Other roles (`listing_copy`, `seller_letter`,
  `disclosure_block`) are not assessed under §4 — note that `disclosure_block` carries
  the disclosure text but is **not** a §4-responsible role.

## 3. Headline numbers

| Metric | Count |
|---|---|
| Sections in inventory (`section_count`) | 30 |
| Flagged — finding not `none` (`flagged_count`) | 19 |
| Sections including `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE` | 7 |
| Sections including `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` | 11 |
| Sections including `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` | 8 |

These count **sections**, not labels: a section carrying several findings is counted once
per metric it trips. Eleven sections are clean (`none`): SEC-01, SEC-06, SEC-10, SEC-12,
SEC-13, SEC-16, SEC-18, SEC-20, SEC-23, SEC-26, SEC-28.

## 4. Findings by rule

### 4.1 PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE — 7 sections

All solicit a buyer personal narrative, independent of role (§1 applies "whatever its
role") and independent of any disclosure exemption (§3 exempts from §2 only):

- **SEC-02** (seller_letter) — "Tell us about yourselves — write us a letter about what
  brought you here and what this home would mean to you."
- **SEC-07** (closing_page) — "Send a personal note about yourself along with the offer;
  the one that moves us most is the one we will take."
- **SEC-08** (disclosure_block) — "We invite buyers to include a short personal note
  about themselves and why this home suits them." (Carries a compliant 11-class notice, so
  no §2/§4 finding, but §1 is unaffected.)
- **SEC-17** (seller_letter) — "Include a covering letter introducing yourself — the
  sellers would like to know who is buying."
- **SEC-24** (closing_page) — "Tell us about yourselves — write us a letter about what
  brought you here…" (Carries a compliant notice; §1 still stands.)
- **SEC-27** (seller_letter) — "Send a personal note about yourself along with the
  offer; the one that moves us most is the one we will take."
- **SEC-29** (agent_bio) — "We invite buyers to include a short personal note about
  themselves and why this home suits them." (Compliant notice; §1 still stands.)

### 4.2 PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE — 11 sections

Two distinct mechanisms produced these.

**(a) Body prose naming §2 classes or proxies** (never coverable by §3):

- **SEC-03** (listing_copy) — "family-oriented street" (familial status proxy), "two
  churches" and "parish school" (religion proxies).
- **SEC-07** (closing_page) — "churchgoing households" (religion), "long-established
  families" (familial status proxy). Also §1 and §4 — see below.
- **SEC-09** (agent_bio) — "young families" (familial status proxy), "parish hall"
  (religion proxy). Also §4 — see below.
- **SEC-17** (seller_letter) — "congregation-centred neighbourhood," "same faith
  community" (religion). Also §1.
- **SEC-19** (closing_page) — body prose "family-oriented street," "churches," "parish
  school" (familial status + religion). Notwithstanding a *compliant* 11-class notice
  carried in the same section: §3 exempts the notice text only, and "protected-class
  terms a section uses in its own prose, outside the notice, are never covered."
- **SEC-25** (listing_copy) — "churchgoing households" (religion), "long-established
  families" (familial status proxy).

**(b) Abridged disclosure notice — no §3 exemption, so the §2 terms inside it count:**

- **SEC-04** (disclosure_block) — carries our standing 9-class notice, missing marital
  status and source of income. Under B1 it is abridged; under §3 an abridged notice earns
  *no* exemption, however official the section looks (it is titled "Fair housing notice").
  Because `disclosure_block` is not a §4-responsible role, there is no `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`
  here — only §2.
- **SEC-11** (closing_page) — same 9-class abridged notice → §2, plus §4 (responsible
  role, abridged notice).
- **SEC-14** (agent_bio) — same 9-class abridged notice → §2, plus §4 (agent_bio is
  responsible from this quarter under B2).
- **SEC-15** (closing_page) — notice names only race, color, religion, sex (4 of 11).
  Heavily abridged → §2, plus §4.
- **SEC-22** (disclosure_block) — legacy notice naming 6 of 11 (missing disability,
  sexual orientation, veteran status, marital status, source of income). Abridged → §2
  only (`disclosure_block` is not §4-responsible).

### 4.3 DISCLAIMER_MISSING — 8 sections

All are in a §4-responsible role (`closing_page` or, from this quarter, `agent_bio`) and
carry **no** compliant notice:

- **SEC-05** (closing_page) — no notice at all.
- **SEC-07** (closing_page) — no notice at all (also §1, §2).
- **SEC-09** (agent_bio) — no notice at all (also §2). Newly in scope under B2.
- **SEC-11** (closing_page) — abridged 9-class notice (also §2).
- **SEC-14** (agent_bio) — abridged 9-class notice (also §2). Newly in scope under B2.
- **SEC-15** (closing_page) — abridged 4-class notice (also §2).
- **SEC-21** (agent_bio) — no notice at all. Newly in scope under B2.
- **SEC-30** (closing_page) — no notice at all.

### 4.4 Sections carrying a compliant 11-class notice that came back clean

For completeness, these carried the full amended notice and tripped no other rule:
SEC-10, SEC-13, SEC-26. (SEC-08, SEC-19, SEC-24, SEC-29 also carry the compliant notice
but trip §1 and/or §2 from their own prose, as noted above.)

## 5. Notes for sign-off

- The single largest source of findings this quarter is **B1**: our standing 9-class
  disclosure paragraph is now abridged wherever it appears. The four sections still
  carrying it (SEC-04, SEC-11, SEC-14, and — in a shorter form — SEC-15) all fail §2, and
  the two of them in responsible roles (SEC-11, SEC-14) also fail §4. Reissuing the
  template to the 11-class form (as SEC-08/10/13/19/24/26/29 already use) would clear the
  §2/§4 findings on the responsible-role sections but would **not** cure §1 or any
  body-prose §2 finding.
- B2 brings three `agent_bio` sections into §4 scope (SEC-09, SEC-14, SEC-21); two of them
  (SEC-09, SEC-14) would not have been assessed at all last year.
- §1 personal-narrative findings are role-independent and cannot be fixed by the
  disclaimer; they require the solicitation language to be removed.
